title: A power law is a straight line on log-log axes
caption: With P(k) ∝ k^−2.5, log₁₀ P(k)/P(10) falls by 2.5 for each tenfold rise in k. From degree 10 to degree 100 it falls by 2.5, so P(100)/P(10) = 10^−2.5 ≈ 0.0032: about 316 times rarer.
alt: A straight line of gradient minus 2.5 on log-log axes from degree 10 (x = 1, y = 0) to degree 100 (x = 2, y = minus 2.5).
description: Take P(k) ∝ k^−2.5 and measure everything against degree 10.
On log axes, log₁₀ P(k)/P(10) = −2.5 (log₁₀ k − 1), a straight line of gradient −2.5.
At degree 100, log₁₀ k = 2, so the line is at −2.5.
That is a ratio of 10^−2.5 ≈ 0.0032: degree 100 is about 316 times rarer than degree 10.
